do.message: Mom told you to clean the gutters. All of them. Twice, because the first time "didn't count".
Mom told you to drive Grandma to Hämeenlinna for her hair appointment. Grandma narrated the whole drive.
Mom told you to help Dad fix the moped. You held a torch for five hours while he swore at a carburettor.
Mom told you to stack the firewood. Then to restack it "properly", like your cousin does.
Mom told you to come to Aunt Raili's birthday. Seven kinds of cake and one question: "So, any plans?"
Mom told you to weed the potato patch. The weeds won. You lost a whole Saturday.
Mom told you to take the rag rugs to the lake and scrub them on the washing pier. It took all day, and a pike watched.
Mom told you to sort the attic. You found your old school reports. So did she.

then.message: You ate the last of your food over the weekend. Restock before next weekend.

else.message: There was no food at home. You spent the weekend hungry and feel weak.

then.message: You were evicted for unpaid rent! Back to your parents' place, and Mom has a list of chores ready.
A note on your door: last month's rent is still unpaid. Another month like that and you're out.

else.message: A new month: rent of €{flag('rent')} is due.

do.message: The basement studio smells of damp again. You can hear Pellinen's keyboard through the wall at all hours.
Your one small window shows ankles. Ankles going to work, ankles coming home. Ankles in the rain.
The boiler next door clanked all night. You dreamt of submarines.

then.message: {ownedBy('cottage_deed')} bought the red cottage, and your lease ends with the sale. You carry your boxes back to your parents' house.
You have nothing decent to wear.
Too much work and too little rest: you feel worn out. Rest at home or go to the sauna.

do.message: The stock market is booming! Your shares rose by €{change}. Juho says it can't last. Juho says that every week.
A Finnish phone company announces something shiny. Your shares jump by €{change}.
The stock market crashed! Your shares lost €{-change}. Pekki nods slowly: "Told you. Everything goes down eventually."
Red numbers on the evening news. Your shares are worth €{-change} less than last week.

setWorld.economy: clamp(world.economy + (rnd() - 0.5) * params.economyVolatility + (1 - world.economy) * params.economyPull, params.economyMin, params.economyMax)

then.message: Your head is full this week. The lesson goes in one ear and out the other.

turnEndChecks.message: There is no food at home. You will go hungry this weekend.

hints: Employers notice who shows up reliably.
Managers are picked from their own staff. Shifts at another workplace don't count for that.
Long work weeks pile up stress. Past a point you wear out: rest, sauna or a lighter week helps.
A well-rested mind learns faster. So does a well-read one.
Better clothes open more doors than you would think.
Money in your pocket attracts the wrong kind of attention.
Nobody stays happy without a little sauna now and then.
Living with your parents is cheap, but it wears on you.
Eating out every week adds up. A kitchen of your own pays for itself.
The city pays well, if you have the papers for it.
Stay too long in one job and someone upstairs may notice you.
Bosses count shifts. Show up often enough and the pay goes up, diploma or not.
A diploma is the quick way up. Years on the shop floor are the slow way. Both work.
You don't always need a course to get a certificate. At the school you can show what you already know.
The house band at the lava is always looking for a voice. They listen at karaoke night.
Some people work for a boss. Some people buy a kiosk.
Shares go up more than savings. They also go down more than savings.
A cottage you don't live in can pay for itself. Summer people pay well.
Not every wise person has a degree. The library is free.
Prices go up and down with the times. So do wages.
Never skip meals. A hungry week is a wasted week.
Old-timers say the furniture factory always needs strong hands.
A summer without a dance at the lava is a summer wasted.
Everyone ends up at the Trokari sooner or later. Even me.
Nobody can cram a whole course into one week. Plan for the long haul.
Appliances lose value the day you carry them home. Land and houses hold theirs.
The best jobs in the village have only one desk. Somebody else may get there first.
Happiness fades a little every week, and the happier you are, the faster it fades.
Money in the bank is safe from pickpockets, and it grows a little.
An evening with Pekki makes anyone's life look good by comparison.
Matti says a coffee break is the best medicine for a hard week. Matti is usually right.
Olli is insufferable, but you'll learn more from him than from any book.
Never split a bill with Juho. But do let him look at your savings.
Pellinen's door is always open. The curtains, never.
